content: 1. If the use of copanlisib cannot be avoided, reduce the dose to 45 mg. Posaconazole increases the levels of dabrafenib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Both desflurane and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Both disopyramide and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dronedarone increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The combination of dronedarone with other QT-prolonging medications is contraindicated due to the risk of additive effects and ventricular arrhythmias, including torsades de pointes. 6. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg orally once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 7. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Both eliglustat and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). Both encorafenib and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib. Both entrectinib and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the erdafitinib dose in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 14. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Both eribulin and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of eszopiclone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase the fedratinib dose to 300 mg/day for 2 weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. 20. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of felbamate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 22. Posaconazole decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for decreased efficacy due to reduced plasma concentrations of active M1 and M2 metabolites. 23. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of flunisolide (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of fluticasone (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects; monitor for signs/symptoms of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. 25. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the incidence/severity of futibatinib toxicities. 26. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Both gilteritinib and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 28. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Both hydroxychloroquine sulfate and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Posaconazole increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with posaconazole suspension (100 mg qDay, 100 mg BID, or 200 mg BID), reduce the ibrutinib dose to 140 mg qDay (for B-cell malignancies) or 280 mg qDay (for GvHD). If coadministered with posaconazole suspension (200 mg TID, 400 mg BID), posaconazole 300 mg IV qDay, or posaconazole delayed-release tablets (300 mg qDay), reduce the ibrutinib dose to 70 mg qDay (for B-cell malignancies) or 140 mg qDay (for GvHD). Resume the previous ibrutinib dose after CYP3A inhibitor discontinuation. 31. Both ibutilide and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow dosage modification recommendations if adverse reactions occur. 33. Both indapamide and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of infigratinib (DSC) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of irinotecan (including liposomal formulations) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Both isoflurane and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg qDay. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg qDay after at least 5 half-lives of the inhibitor. Both ivosidenib and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ketamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior larotrectinib dose once the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. 40. Lasmiditan increases the levels of posaconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 42. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 43. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase to the previous lorlatinib dose after 3 plasma half-lives of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 45. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for 5 half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before coadministration. 47. Both macimorelin and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by approximately 11 msec. Avoid coadministration with QT-prolonging drugs to reduce the risk of torsades de pointes. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 48. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of posaconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 50. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of midazolam (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases midazolam systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 51. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor midostaurin for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 52. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 53. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
